When it solves a complex problem, discovers a workflow, or gets corrected, it can persist that knowledge as a skill document that loads into future sessions. Skills accumulate over time, making the agent better at your specific tasks and environment.\n- **Persistent memory across sessions** — remembers who you are, your preferences, environment details, and lessons learned. [command]\n\n  --version, -V             Show version\n  --resume, -r SESSION      Resume session by ID or title\n  --continue, -c [NAME]     Resume by name, or most recent session\n  --worktree, -w            Isolated git worktree mode (parallel agents)\n  --skills, -s SKILL        Preload skills (comma-separate or repeat)\n  --profile, -p NAME        Use a named profile\n  --yolo                    Skip dangerous command approval\n  --pass-session-id         Include session ID in system prompt\n```\n\nNo subcommand defaults to `chat`.\n\n### Chat\n\n```\nhermes chat [flags]\n  -q, --query TEXT          Single query, non-interactive\n  -m, --model MODEL         Model (e.g. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4)\n  -t, --toolsets LIST       Comma-separated toolsets\n  --provider PROVIDER       Force (model|terminal|gateway|tools|agent)\nhermes model                Interactive model/provider picker\nhermes config               View current config\nhermes config edit          Open config.yaml in missing/outdated config\nhermes config migrate       Update config with new options\nhermes login [--provider P] OAuth login (nous, openai-codex)\nhermes logout               Clear stored auth\nhermes doctor [--fix]       Check dependencies and config\nhermes status [--all]       Show component status\n```\n\n### Tools & Skills\n\n```\nhermes tools                Interactive tool enable/disable         Remove last exchange\n/title [name]        Name the session\n/compress            Manually compress context\n/stop                Kill background processes\n/rollback [N]        Restore https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration\n\n### Model Routing Governance\n\nLexi uses a multi-tier model routing system to balance cost and safety. The governance policy lives at:\n\n**`autonomous/protocols/model_routing_policy.md`** (in the Noa-Hermes repo)\n\nFour tiers exist:\n\n| Tier | Model ID | Input $/M | Output $/M | Context |\n|------|----------|-----------|------------|---------|\n| HEAVY | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` | $0.435 | $0.87 | 1M |\n| LIGHT | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` | $0.112 | $0.224 | 1M |\n| FREE | `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash:free` | $0 | $0 | 1M |\n| FALLBACK | `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | $0.10 | $0.40 | 1M |\n\n**Routing principle:** cost saving never reduces safety. When in doubt, always choose HEAVY or ask Lexi.\n\n**Plain-language hard rule (from policy §12 — finalized 2026-05-18):**\n- Flash mag werken.\n- Pro moet beslissen.\n- Free mag alleen rommel zonder risico.\n- Lexi beslist bij twijfel.\n\n**HEAVY (v4-pro)** is mandatory for: Controller/QA/Critic/Strategist decisions, git operations, config changes, secrets, agent/protocol file edits, RUN_STATE changes, scope transitions, install/delete commands, and anything requiring Lexi approval.\n\n**LIGHT (v4-flash, paid)** is the default for: daily chat, read-only analysis, summarization, brainstorming, scout/producer output, simple markdown edits, non-sensitive tasks.\n\n**FREE (v4-flash:free)** is restricted to: public text, title variants, non-sensitive brainstorming without repo context — never for repo content, system files, or personal data.\n\n**FALLBACK (gemini-flash-lite)** is for: DeepSeek failures, specific multimodal tasks, not standard governance.\n\n**Finance Guard expanded reporting** (applies alongside every routing decision):\n- Report: chosen model, reason, cost tier (free/low/medium/high/unknown), whether Lexi approval is needed, whether the task creates recurring cost, and whether sensitive data would go to a free/light model.\n- Finance Guard must NOT: change providers, change models, modify config, commit/push, or decide on Lexi's behalf.\n\n**Setting the default model:**\n```bash\nhermes config set model.default deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash\n```\n\n**Setting auxiliary models:**\n```bash\nhermes config set auxiliary.triage_specifier.model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash\nhermes config set auxiliary.title_generation.model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash\n```\n\n**Warning:** Do NOT set `approval`, `skills_hub`, `curator`, `kanban_decomposer`, or `mcp` auxiliary models to light/free without separate Lexi approval.\n\n**Implementation order:** create policy file → update Controller reference → switch default model → document heavy override → test → set auxiliary slots.\n\n### Providers\n\n20+ providers supported. platforms inherit from.\n\nTool changes take effect on `/reset` (new session). They do NOT apply mid-conversation to preserve prompt caching.\n\n---\n\n## Security & Privacy Toggles\n\nCommon \"why is Hermes doing X to my output / tool calls / commands?\" toggles — and the exact commands to change them. Most of these need a fresh session (`/reset` in chat, or start a new `hermes` invocation) because they're read once at startup.\n\n### Secret redaction in tool output\n\nSecret redaction is **off by default** — tool output (terminal stdout, `read_file`, web content, subagent summaries, etc.) passes through unmodified. If the user wants Hermes to auto-mask strings that look like API keys, tokens, and secrets before they enter the conversation context and logs:\n\n```bash\nhermes config set security.redact_secrets true       # enable globally\n```\n\n**Restart required.** `security.redact_secrets` is snapshotted at import time — toggling it mid-session (e.g. via `export HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS=true` from a tool call) will NOT take effect for the running process. Tell the user to run `hermes config set security.redact_secrets true` in a terminal, then start a new session. This is deliberate — it prevents an LLM from flipping the toggle on itself mid-task.\n\nDisable again with:\n```bash\nhermes config set security.redact_secrets false\n```\n\n### PII redaction in gateway messages\n\nSeparate from secret redaction. When enabled, the gateway hashes user IDs and strips phone numbers from the session context before it reaches the model:\n\n```bash\nhermes config set privacy.redact_pii true    # enable\nhermes config set privacy.redact_pii false   # disable (default)\n```\n\n### Command approval prompts\n\nBy default (`approvals.mode: manual`), Hermes prompts the user before running shell commands flagged as destructive (`rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, etc.). The modes are:\n\n- `manual` — always prompt (default)\n- `smart` — use an auxiliary LLM to auto-approve low-risk commands, prompt on high-risk\n- `off` — skip all approval prompts (equivalent to `--yolo`)\n\n```bash\nhermes config set approvals.mode smart       # recommended middle ground\nhermes config set approvals.mode off         # bypass everything (not recommended)\n```\n\nPer-invocation bypass without changing config:\n- `hermes --yolo …`\n- `export HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1`\n\nNote: YOLO / `approvals.mode: off` does NOT turn off secret redaction. They are independent.\n\n### Shell hooks allowlist\n\nSome shell-hook integrations require explicit allowlisting before they fire. Managed via `~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json` — prompted interactively the first time a hook wants to run.\n\n### Disabling the web/browser/image-gen tools\n\nTo keep the model away from network or media tools entirely, open `hermes tools` and toggle per-platform. Takes effect on next session (`/reset`). See the Tools & Skills section above.\n\n---\n\n## Voice & Transcription\n\n### STT (Voice → Text)\n\nVoice messages from messaging platforms are auto-transcribed.\n\nProvider priority (auto-detected):\n1. **Local faster-whisper** — free, no API key: `pip install faster-whisper`\n2. **Groq Whisper** — free tier: set `GROQ_API_KEY`\n3. **OpenAI Whisper** — paid: set `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY`\n4. **Mistral Voxtral** — set `MISTRAL_API_KEY`\n\nConfig:\n```yaml\nstt:\n  enabled: true\n  provider: local        # local, groq, openai, mistral\n  local:\n    model: base          # tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3\n```\n\n### TTS (Text → Voice)\n\n| Provider | Env var | Free? |\n|----------|---------|-------|\n| Edge TTS | None | Yes (default) |\n| ElevenLabs | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | Free tier |\n| OpenAI | `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY` | Paid |\n| MiniMax | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` | Paid |\n| Mistral (Voxtral) | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` | Paid |\n| NeuTTS (local) | None (`pip install neutts[all]` + `espeak-ng`) | Free |\n\nVoice commands: `/voice on` (voice-to-voice), `/voice tts` (always voice), `/voice off`.\n\n---\n\n## Spawning Additional Hermes Instances\n\nRun additional Hermes processes as fully independent subprocesses — separate sessions, tools, and environments.\n\n### When to Use This vs delegate_task\n\n| | `delegate_task` | Spawning `hermes` process |\n|-|-----------------|--------------------------|\n| Isolation | Separate conversation, shared process | Fully independent process |\n| Duration | Minutes (bounded by parent loop) | Hours/days |\n| Tool access | Subset of parent's tools | Full tool access |\n| Interactive | No | Yes (PTY mode) |\n| Use case | Quick parallel subtasks | Long autonomous missions |\n\n### One-Shot Mode\n\n```\nterminal(command=\"hermes chat -q 'Research GRPO papers and write summary to ~/research/grpo.md'\", timeout=300)\n\n# Background for long tasks:\nterminal(command=\"hermes chat -q 'Set up CI/CD for ~/myapp'\", background=true)\n```\n\n### Interactive PTY Mode (via tmux)\n\nHermes uses prompt_toolkit, which requires a real terminal. Use tmux for interactive spawning:\n\n```\n# Start\nterminal(command=\"tmux new-session -d -s agent1 -x 120 -y 40 'hermes'\", timeout=10)\n\n# Wait for startup, then send a message\nterminal(command=\"sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t agent1 'Build a FastAPI auth service' Enter\", timeout=15)\n\n# Read output\nterminal(command=\"sleep 20 && tmux capture-pane -t agent1 -p\", timeout=5)\n\n# Send follow-up\nterminal(command=\"tmux send-keys -t agent1 'Add rate limiting middleware' Enter\", timeout=5)\n\n# Exit\nterminal(command=\"tmux send-keys -t agent1 '/exit' Enter && sleep 2 && tmux kill-session -t agent1\", timeout=10)\n```\n\n### Multi-Agent Coordination\n\n```\n# Agent A: backend\nterminal(command=\"tmux new-session -d -s backend -x 120 -y 40 'hermes -w'\", timeout=10)\nterminal(command=\"sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t backend 'Build REST API for user management' Enter\", timeout=15)\n\n# Agent B: frontend\nterminal(command=\"tmux new-session -d -s frontend -x 120 -y 40 'hermes -w'\", timeout=10)\nterminal(command=\"sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t frontend 'Build React dashboard for user management' Enter\", timeout=15)\n\n# Check progress, relay context between them\nterminal(command=\"tmux capture-pane -t backend -p | tail -30\", timeout=5)\nterminal(command=\"tmux send-keys -t frontend 'Here is the API schema from the backend agent: ...' Enter\", timeout=5)\n```\n\n### Session Resume\n\n```\n# Resume most recent session\nterminal(command=\"tmux new-session -d -s resumed 'hermes --continue'\", timeout=10)\n\n# Resume specific session\nterminal(command=\"tmux new-session -d -s resumed 'hermes --resume 20260225_143052_a1b2c3'\", timeout=10)\n```\n\n### Tips\n\n- **Prefer `delegate_task` for quick subtasks** — less overhead than spawning a full process\n- **Use `-w` (worktree mode)** when spawning agents that edit code — prevents git conflicts\n- **Set timeouts** for one-shot mode — complex tasks can take 5-10 minutes\n- **Use `hermes chat -q` for fire-and-forget** — no PTY needed\n- **Use tmux for interactive sessions** — raw PTY mode has `\\r` vs `\\n` issues with prompt_toolkit\n- **For scheduled tasks**, use the `cronjob` tool instead of spawning — handles delivery and retry\n\n---\n\n## Durable & Background Systems\n\nFour systems run alongside the main conversation loop. Quick reference\nhere; full developer notes live in `AGENTS.md`, user-facing docs under\n`website/docs/user-guide/features/`.\n\n### Delegation (`delegate_task`)\n\nSynchronous subagent spawn — the parent waits for the child's summary\nbefore continuing its own loop. Isolated context + terminal session.\n\n- **Single:** `delegate_task(goal, context, toolsets)`.\n- **Batch:** `delegate_task(tasks=[{goal, ...}, ...])` runs children in\n  parallel, capped by `delegation.max_concurrent_children` (default 3).\n- **Roles:** `leaf` (default; cannot re-delegate) vs `orchestrator`\n  (can spawn its own workers, bounded by `delegation.max_spawn_depth`).\n- **Not durable.** If the parent is interrupted, the child is\n  cancelled. For work that must outlive the turn, use `cronjob` or\n  `terminal(background=True, notify_on_complete=True)`.\n\nConfig: `delegation.*` in `config.yaml`.\n\n### Cron (scheduled jobs)\n\nDurable scheduler — `cron/jobs.py` + `cron/scheduler.py`. Drive it via\nthe `cronjob` tool, the `hermes cron` CLI (`list`, `add`, `edit`,\n`pause`, `resume`, `run`, `remove`), or the `/cron` slash command.\n\n- **Schedules:** duration (`\"30m\"`, `\"2h\"`), \"every\" phrase\n  (`\"every monday 9am\"`), 5-field cron (`\"0 9 * * *\"`), or ISO timestamp.\n- **Per-job knobs:** `skills`, `model`/`provider` override, `script`\n  (pre-run data collection; `no_agent=True` makes the script the whole\n  job), `context_from` (chain job A's output into job B), `workdir`\n  (run in a specific dir with its `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` loaded),\n  multi-platform delivery.\n- **Invariants:** 3-minute hard interrupt per run, `.tick.lock` file\n  prevents duplicate ticks across processes, cron sessions pass\n  `skip_memory=True` by default, and cron deliveries are framed with a\n  header/footer instead of being mirrored into the target gateway\n  session (keeps role alternation intact).\n\nUser docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron\n\n### Curator (skill lifecycle)\n\nBackground maintenance for agent-created skills. Tracks usage, marks\nidle skills stale, archives stale ones, keeps a pre-run tar.gz backup\nso nothing is lost.\n\n- **CLI:** `hermes curator <verb>` — `status`, `run`, `pause`, `resume`,\n  `pin`, `unpin`, `archive`, `restore`, `prune`, `backup`, `rollback`.\n- **Slash:** `/curator <subcommand>` mirrors the CLI.\n- **Scope:** only touches skills with `created_by: \"agent\"` provenance.\n  Bundled + hub-installed skills are off-limits. **Never deletes** —\n  max destructive action is archive. Pinned skills are exempt from\n  every auto-transition and every LLM review pass.\n- **Telemetry:** sidecar at `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json` holds\n  per-skill `use_count`, `view_count`, `patch_count`,\n  `last_activity_at`, `state`, `pinned`.\n\nConfig: `curator.*` (`enabled`, `interval_hours`, `min_idle_hours`,\n`stale_after_days`, `archive_after_days`, `backup.*`).\nUser docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/curator\n\n### Kanban (multi-agent work queue)\n\nDurable SQLite board for multi-profile / multi-worker collaboration.\nUsers drive it via `hermes kanban <verb>`; dispatcher-spawned workers\nsee a focused `kanban_*` toolset gated by `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` so the\nschema footprint is zero outside worker processes.\n\n- **CLI verbs (common):** `init`, `create`, `list` (alias `ls`),\n  `show`, `assign`, `link`, `unlink`, `comment`, `complete`, `block`,\n  `unblock`, `archive`, `tail`. Less common: `watch`, `stats`, `runs`,\n  `log`, `dispatch`, `daemon`, `gc`.\n- **Worker toolset:** `kanban_show`, `kanban_complete`, `kanban_block`,\n  `kanban_heartbeat`, `kanban_comment`, `kanban_create`, `kanban_link`.\n- **Dispatcher** runs inside the gateway by default\n  (`kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true`) — reclaims stale claims,\n  promotes ready tasks, atomically claims, spawns assigned profiles.\n  Auto-blocks a task after ~5 consecutive spawn failures.\n- **Isolation:** board is the hard boundary (workers get\n  `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` pinned in env); tenant is a soft namespace\n  within a board for workspace-path + memory-key isolation.\n\nUser docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/kanban\n\n---\n\n## Windows-Specific Quirks\n\nHermes runs natively on Windows (PowerShell, cmd, Windows Terminal, git-bash\nmintty, VS Code integrated terminal). Most of it just works, but a handful\nof differences between Win32 and POSIX have bitten us — document new ones\nhere as you hit them so the next person (or the next session) doesn't\nrediscover them from scratch.\n\n### Input / Keybindings\n\n**Alt+Enter doesn't insert a newline.** Windows Terminal intercepts Alt+Enter\nat the terminal layer to toggle fullscreen — the keystroke never reaches\nprompt_toolkit. Use **Ctrl+Enter** instead. Windows Terminal delivers\nCtrl+Enter as LF (`c-j`), distinct from plain Enter (`c-m` / CR), and the\nCLI binds `c-j` to newline insertion on `win32` only (see\n`_bind_prompt_submit_keys` + the Windows-only `c-j` binding in `cli.py`).\nSide effect: the raw Ctrl+J keystroke also inserts a newline on Windows —\nunavoidable, because Windows Terminal collapses Ctrl+Enter and Ctrl+J to\nthe same keycode at the Win32 console API layer. No conflicting binding\nexisted for Ctrl+J on Windows, so this is a harmless side effect.\n\nmintty / git-bash behaves the same (fullscreen on Alt+Enter) unless you\ndisable Alt+Fn shortcuts in Options → Keys. Easier to just use Ctrl+Enter.\n\n**Diagnosing keybindings.** Run `python scripts/keystroke_diagnostic.py`\n(repo root) to see exactly how prompt_toolkit identifies each keystroke\nin the current terminal. Answers questions like \"does Shift+Enter come\nthrough as a distinct key?\" (almost never — most terminals collapse it\nto plain Enter) or \"what byte sequence is my terminal sending for\nCtrl+Enter?\" This is how the Ctrl+Enter = c-j fact was established.\n\n### Config / Files\n\n**HTTP 400 \"No models provided\" on first run.** `config.yaml` was saved\nwith a UTF-8 BOM (common when Windows apps write it). Re-save as UTF-8\nwithout BOM. `hermes config edit` writes without BOM; manual edits in\nNotepad are the usual culprit.\n\n### `execute_code` / Sandbox\n\n**WinError 10106** (\"The requested service provider could not be loaded\nor initialized\") from the sandbox child process — it can't create an\n`AF_INET` socket, so the loopback-TCP RPC fallback fails before\n`connect()`. Root cause is usually **not** a broken Winsock LSP; it's\nHermes's own env scrubber dropping `SYSTEMROOT` / `WINDIR` / `COMSPEC`\nfrom the child env. Python's `socket` module needs `SYSTEMROOT` to locate\n`mswsock.dll`. Fixed via the `_WINDOWS_ESSENTIAL_ENV_VARS` allowlist in\n`tools/code_execution_tool.py`. If you still hit it, echo `os.environ`\ninside an `execute_code` block to confirm `SYSTEMROOT` is set. Full\ndiagnostic recipe in `references/execute-code-sandbox-env-windows.md`.\n\n### Testing / Contributing\n\n**`scripts/run_tests.sh` doesn't work as-is on Windows** — it looks for\nPOSIX venv layouts (`.venv/bin/activate`). The Hermes-installed venv at\n`venv/Scripts/` has no pip or pytest either (stripped for install size).\nWorkaround: install `pytest + pytest-xdist + pyyaml` into a system Python\n3.11 user site, then invoke pytest directly with `PYTHONPATH` set:\n\n```bash\n\"/c/Program Files/Python311/python\" -m pip install --user pytest pytest-xdist pyyaml\nexport PYTHONPATH=\"$(pwd)\"\n\"/c/Program Files/Python311/python\" -m pytest tests/foo/test_bar.py -v --tb=short -n 0\n```\n\nUse `-n 0`, not `-n 4` — `pyproject.toml`'s default `addopts` already\nincludes `-n`, and the wrapper's CI-parity guarantees don't apply off POSIX.\n\n**POSIX-only tests need skip guards.** Common markers already in the codebase:\n- Symlinks — elevated privileges on Windows\n- `0o600` file modes — POSIX mode bits not enforced on NTFS by default\n- `signal.SIGALRM` — Unix-only (see `tests/conftest.py::_enforce_test_timeout`)\n- Winsock / Windows-specific regressions — `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != \"win32\", ...)`\n\nUse the existing skip-pattern style (`sys.platform == \"win32\"` or\n`sys.platform.startswith(\"win\")`) to stay consistent with the rest of the\nsuite.\n\n### Path / Filesystem\n\n**Line endings.** Git may warn `LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time\nGit touches it`. Cosmetic — the repo's `.gitattributes` normalizes. Don't\nlet editors auto-convert committed POSIX-newline files to CRLF.\n\n**Forward slashes work almost everywhere.** `C:/Users/...` is accepted by\nevery Hermes tool and most Windows APIs. Prefer forward slashes in code\nand logs — avoids shell-escaping backslashes in bash.\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Voice not working\n1. Check `stt.enabled: true` in config.yaml\n2. Verify provider: `pip install faster-whisper` or set API key\n3. In gateway: `/restart`. In CLI: exit and relaunch.\n\n### Tool not available\n1. `hermes tools` — check if toolset is enabled for your platform\n2. Some tools need env vars (check `.env`)\n3. `/reset` after enabling tools\n\n### Model/provider issues\n1. `hermes doctor` — check config and dependencies\n2. `hermes login` — re-authenticate OAuth providers\n3. Check `.env` has the right API key\n4. **Copilot 403**: `gh auth login` tokens do NOT work for Copilot API. You must use the Copilot-specific OAuth device code flow via `hermes model` → GitHub Copilot.\n\n### Changes not taking effect\n- **Tools/skills:** `/reset` starts a new session with updated toolset\n- **Config changes:** In gateway: `/restart`. In CLI: exit and relaunch.\n- **Code changes:** Restart the CLI or gateway process\n\n### Skills not showing\n1. `hermes skills list` — verify installed\n2. `hermes skills config` — check platform enablement\n3. Load explicitly: `/skill name` or `hermes -s name`\n\n### Gateway issues\nCheck logs first:\n```bash\ngrep -i \"failed to send\\|error\" ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log | tail -20\n```\n\nCommon gateway problems:\n- **Gateway dies on SSH logout**: Enable linger: `sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER`\n- **Gateway dies on WSL2 close**: WSL2 requires `systemd=true` in `/etc/wsl.conf` for systemd services to work. Without it, gateway falls back to `nohup` (dies when session closes).\n- **Gateway crash loop**: Reset the failed state: `systemctl --user reset-failed hermes-gateway`\n\n### Platform-specific issues\n- **Discord bot silent**: Must enable **Message Content Intent** in Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents.\n- **Slack bot only works in DMs**: Must subscribe to `message.channels` event. Without it, the bot ignores public channels.\n- **Windows-specific issues** (`Alt+Enter` newline, WinError 10106, UTF-8 BOM config, test suite, line endings): see the dedicated **Windows-Specific Quirks** section above.\n\n### Auxiliary models not working\nIf `auxiliary` tasks (vision, compression, session_search) fail silently, the `auto` provider can't find a backend. Either set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, or explicitly configure each auxiliary task's provider:\n```bash\nhermes config set auxiliary.vision.provider <your_provider>\nhermes config set auxiliary.vision.model <model_name>\n```\n\n---\n\n## Where to Find Things\n\n| Looking for... | Location |\n|----------------|----------|\n| Config options | `hermes config edit` or [Configuration docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration) |\n| Available tools | `hermes tools list` or [Tools reference](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/tools-reference) |\n| Slash commands | `/help` in session or [Slash commands reference](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/slash-commands) |\n| Skills catalog | `hermes skills browse` or [Skills catalog](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/skills-catalog) |\n| Provider setup | `hermes model` or [Providers guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers) |\n| Platform setup | `hermes gateway setup` or [Messaging docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/) |\n| MCP servers | `hermes mcp list` or [MCP guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp) |\n| Profiles | `hermes profile list` or [Profiles docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/profiles) |\n| Cron jobs | `hermes cron list` or [Cron docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron) |\n| Memory | `hermes memory status` or [Memory docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/memory) |\n| Env variables | `hermes config env-path` or [Env vars reference](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/environment-variables) |\n| CLI commands | `hermes --help` or [CLI reference](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands) |\n| Gateway logs | `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` |\n| Session files | `~/.hermes/sessions/` or `hermes sessions browse` |\n| Source code | `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/` |\n\n---\n\n## Contributor Quick Reference\n\nFor occasional contributors and PR authors. Full developer docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/\n\n### Project Layout\n\n```\nhermes-agent/\n├── run_agent.py          # AIAgent — core conversation loop\n├── model_tools.py        # Tool discovery and dispatch\n├── toolsets.py           # Toolset definitions\n├── cli.py                # Interactive CLI (HermesCLI)\n├── hermes_state.py       # SQLite session store\n├── agent/                # Prompt builder, context compression, memory, model routing, credential pooling, skill dispatch\n├── hermes_cli/           # CLI subcommands, config, setup, commands\n│   ├── commands.py       # Slash command registry (CommandDef)\n│   ├── config.py         # DEFAULT_CONFIG, env var definitions\n│   └── main.py           # CLI entry point and argparse\n├── tools/                # One file per tool\n│   └── registry.py       # Central tool registry\n├── gateway/              # Messaging gateway\n│   └── platforms/        # Platform adapters (telegram, discord, etc.)\n├── cron/                 # Job scheduler\n├── tests/                # ~3000 pytest tests\n└── website/              # Docusaurus docs site\n```\n\nConfig: `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (settings), `~/.hermes/.env` (API keys).\n\n### Adding a Tool (3 files)\n\n**1. Create `tools/your_tool.py`:**\n```python\nimport json, os\nfrom tools.registry import registry\n\ndef check_requirements() -> bool:\n    return bool(os.getenv(\"EXAMPLE_API_KEY\"))\n\ndef example_tool(param: str, task_id: str = None) -> str:\n    return json.dumps({\"success\": True, \"data\": \"...\"})\n\nregistry.register(\n    name=\"example_tool\",\n    toolset=\"example\",\n    schema={\"name\": \"example_tool\", \"description\": \"...\", \"parameters\": {...}},\n    handler=lambda args, **kw: example_tool(\n        param=args.get(\"param\", \"\"), task_id=kw.get(\"task_id\")),\n    check_fn=check_requirements,\n    requires_env=[\"EXAMPLE_API_KEY\"],\n)\n```\n\n**2. Add to `toolsets.py`** → `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS` list.\n\nAuto-discovery: any `tools/*.py` file with a top-level `registry.register()` call is imported automatically — no manual list needed.\n\nAll handlers must return JSON strings. Use `get_hermes_home()` for paths, never hardcode `~/.hermes`.\n\n### Adding a Slash Command\n\n1. Add `CommandDef` to `COMMAND_REGISTRY` in `hermes_cli/commands.py`\n2. Add handler in `cli.py` → `process_command()`\n3. (Optional) Add gateway handler in `gateway/run.py`\n\nAll consumers (help text, autocomplete, Telegram menu, Slack mapping) derive from the central registry automatically.\n\n### Agent Loop (High Level)\n\n```\nrun_conversation():\n  1. Build system prompt\n  2. Loop while iterations < max:\n     a. Call LLM (OpenAI-format messages + tool schemas)\n     b. If tool_calls → dispatch each via handle_function_call() → append results → continue\n     c. If text response → return\n  3. Context compression triggers automatically near token limit\n```\n\n### Testing\n\n```bash\npython -m pytest tests/ -o 'addopts=' -q   # Full suite\npython -m pytest tests/tools/ -q            # Specific area\n```\n\n- Tests auto-redirect `HERMES_HOME` to temp dirs — never touch real `~/.hermes/`\n- Run full suite before pushing any change\n- Use `-o 'addopts='` to clear any baked-in pytest flags\n\n**Windows contributors:** `scripts/run_tests.sh` currently looks for POSIX venvs (`.venv/bin/activate` / `venv/bin/activate`) and will error out on Windows where the layout is `venv/Scripts/activate` + `python.exe`. The Hermes-installed venv at `venv/Scripts/` also has no `pip` or `pytest` — it's stripped for end-user install size. Workaround: install pytest + pytest-xdist + pyyaml into a system Python 3.11 user site (`/c/Program Files/Python311/python -m pip install --user pytest pytest-xdist pyyaml`), then run tests directly:\n\n```bash\nexport PYTHONPATH=\"$(pwd)\"\n\"/c/Program Files/Python311/python\" -m pytest tests/tools/test_foo.py -v --tb=short -n 0\n```\n\nUse `-n 0` (not `-n 4`) because `pyproject.toml`'s default `addopts` already includes `-n`, and the wrapper's CI-parity story doesn't apply off-POSIX.\n\n**Cross-platform test guards:** tests that use POSIX-only syscalls need a skip marker. Common ones already in the codebase:\n- Symlink creation → `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == \"win32\", reason=\"Symlinks require elevated privileges on Windows\")` (see `tests/cron/test_cron_script.py`)\n- POSIX file modes (0o600, etc.) → `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform.startswith(\"win\"), reason=\"POSIX mode bits not enforced on Windows\")` (see `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_toctou_file_modes.py`)\n- `signal.SIGALRM` → Unix-only (see `tests/conftest.py::_enforce_test_timeout`)\n- Live Winsock / Windows-specific regression tests → `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != \"win32\", reason=\"Windows-specific regression\")`\n\n**Monkeypatching `sys.platform` is not enough** when the code under test also calls `platform.system()` / `platform.release()` / `platform.mac_ver()`. Those functions re-read the real OS independently, so a test that sets `sys.platform = \"linux\"` on a Windows runner will still see `platform.system() == \"Windows\"` and route through the Windows branch. Patch all three together:\n\n```python\nmonkeypatch.setattr(sys, \"platform\", \"linux\")\nmonkeypatch.setattr(platform, \"system\", lambda: \"Linux\")\nmonkeypatch.setattr(platform, \"release\", lambda: \"6.8.0-generic\")\n```\n\nSee `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py::TestEnvironmentHints` for a worked example.\n\n### Extending the system prompt's execution-environment block\n\nFactual guidance about the host OS, user home, cwd, terminal backend, and shell (bash vs. PowerShell on Windows) is emitted from `agent/prompt_builder.py::build_environment_hints()`. This is also where the WSL hint and per-backend probe logic live. The convention:\n\n- **Local terminal backend** → emit host info (OS, `$HOME`, cwd) + Windows-specific notes (hostname ≠ username, `terminal` uses bash not PowerShell).\n- **Remote terminal backend** (anything in `_REMOTE_TERMINAL_BACKENDS`: `docker, singularity, modal, daytona, ssh, vercel_sandbox, managed_modal`) → **suppress** host info entirely and describe only the backend. A live `uname`/`whoami`/`pwd` probe runs inside the backend via `tools.environments.get_environment(...).execute(...)`, cached per process in `_BACKEND_PROBE_CACHE`, with a static fallback if the probe times out.\n- **Key fact for prompt authoring:** when `TERMINAL_ENV != \"local\"`, *every* file tool (`read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`) runs inside the backend container, not on the host. The system prompt must never describe the host in that case — the agent can't touch it.\n\nFull design notes, the exact emitted strings, and testing pitfalls:\n`references/prompt-builder-environment-hints.md`.\n\n**Refactor-safety pattern (POSIX-equivalence guard):** when you extract inline logic into a helper that adds Windows/platform-specific behavior, keep a `_legacy_<name>` oracle function in the test file that's a verbatim copy of the old code, then parametrize-diff against it. Example: `tests/tools/test_code_execution_windows_env.py::TestPosixEquivalence`. This locks in the invariant that POSIX behavior is bit-for-bit identical and makes any future drift fail loudly with a clear diff.\n\n### Commit Conventions\n\n```\ntype: concise subject line\n\nOptional body.\n```\n\nTypes: `fix:`, `feat:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `chore:`\nThis locks in the invariant that POSIX behavior is bit-for-bit identical and makes any future drift fail loudly with a clear diff.\n\n# Noa Second Brain Workflow\nSee `references/second-brain-ingestion.md` for details on the knowledge ingestion process.\n\n## Key Rules & Practices\n\n- **Second Brain Entry Types:**\n    - `concept`\n    - `entity`\n    - `source_summary`\n    - `synthesis`\n    - `log`\n    - `index`\n    - `project`\n    - `fix`\n    - `decision`\n- **ECGT Principle:** The term \"ECGT\" (Eerst Controleren, Daarna Garanderen, Transparant Afhandelen) has been defined and is to be applied following Lexi's explicit confirmation for usage rules. It emphasizes accountability and transparency in operations. Consistency and explicit user approval are key. Memory entries related to its definition are updated accordingly.\n\n- **General Workflow Rules:**\n    - Never break prompt caching (don't change context, tools, or system prompt mid-conversation).\n    - Maintain message role alternation (never two assistant or two user messages in a row).\n    - Use `get_hermes_home()` from `hermes_constants` for all paths (profile-safe).\n    - Config values go in `config.yaml`, secrets go in `.env`.\n    - New tools need a `check_fn` so they only appear when requirements are met.\n## AI Development and Self-Reflection\n\n- `references/noa_self_understanding.md`: Details of Noa's self-understanding derived from the Hermes Agent framework.\n- `references/system-prompt-architecture.md`: How SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, .hermes.md, memory, and skills are loaded into the system prompt — with source code locations and priority chain.\n", "path": "autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent/SKILL.md", "skill_dir": "/home/sjoe/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent", "org_provenance": null, "linked_files": {"references": ["references/noa_self_understanding.md", "references/system-prompt-architecture.md", "references/second-brain-ingestion.md"]}, "usage_hint": "To view linked files, call skill_view(name, file_path) where file_path is e.g. 'references/api.md' or 'assets/config.yaml'", "required_environment_variables": [], "required_commands": [], "missing_required_environment_variables": [], "missing_credential_files": [], "missing_required_commands": [], "setup_needed": false, "setup_skipped": false, "readiness_status": "available", "_source_path": "/home/sjoe/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent/SKILL.md", "metadata": {"hermes": {"tags": ["hermes", "setup", "configuration", "multi-agent", "spawning", "cli", "gateway", "development"], "homepage": "https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent", "related_skills": ["claude-code", "codex", "opencode"]}}}

- `hermes gateway restart` → graceful restart, nieuwe PID 956674.
- Geverifieerd: gateway draait nu op verse code, geen `line_input`-fout meer.
- Telegram is terug verbonden: "Connected to Telegram (polling mode)" + "polling confirmed healthy".

De MCP-servers `filesystem` en `health-monitor` falen bij connectie ("Connection closed"), al dagen, om de ~5 min opnieuw. Dat was er al vóór de update en is niet opgelost door de herstart. Dat is een apart probleem — zeg maar of ik daar in moet duiken, dan pak ik het los aan.

### Assistant — 2026-08-25T06:19:56.014807Z

Analyse compleet, Lexi. Twee aparte problemen, beide los van de update. Hier het bewijs:

PROBLEEM 1 — health-monitor: betere-sqlite3 ABI-mismatch

Uit `~/.hermes/logs/mcp-stderr.log`:

```
[mcp-server-health-monitor] Fatal error: The module '...better_sqlite3/build/Release/better_sqlite3.node'
was compiled against NODE_MODULE_VERSION 137. This version of Node.js requires NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127.
```

Root cause: twee Node-versies op je server die door elkaar lopen.
- Systeem-node: `/usr/bin/node` = v24.16.0 (ABI 137)
- Hermes-bundled node: `/home/sjoe/.hermes/node/bin/node` = v22.23.2 (ABI 127)

De gateway (systemd user service) heeft `/home/sjoe/.hermes/node/bin` VOOR `/usr/bin` in z'n PATH (zie `hermes-gateway.service`). Dus `command: node` in de health-monitor-config laadt de Hermes-node v22 (ABI 127), maar `better_sqlite3.node` is ooit gecompileerd voor v24 (ABI 137). Vandaar de crash bij elke connectiepoging.

PROBLEEM 2 — filesystem: config-bug met dubbele `--args`

Uit `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (regel 667-681):

```yaml
filesystem:
  command: npx
  args:
    - -y
    - --args              ← fout
    - '@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem'
    - --args              ← fout
    - /home/sjoe/system/hermes-second-brain
    - --args              ← fout
    ... (5× in totaal)
```

npm krijgt letterlijk `--args` als CLI-flag binnen en crasht: `npm error Unknown cli flag: --args`. Het token `--args` hoort daar niet — de correcte vorm is gewoon `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <pad1> <pad2> ...`.

VOORSTELLENDE FIX (nog niet uitgevoerd — jij beslist):

1. health-monitor: rebuild de native module tegen de juiste node:
   `cd /home/sjoe/.hermes/mcp-local/mcp-health-monitor && /home/sjoe/.hermes/node/bin/npm rebuild better-sqlite3`
2. filesystem: verwijder de 5 `--args`-tokens uit config.yaml, allowlist-paden verbatim behouden (die zijn conform je MCP-beveiligingsregel: max `/home/sjoe/.hermes/skills`).

Opmerking: je allowlist staat nu op `hermes-second-brain`, `Noa-Hermes`, `scripts` en `.hermes/skills` — dat laat ik bij de fix exact zoals het is.

Zeg "doe maar" en ik voer beide fixes uit en test de connectie.

### Assistant — 2026-08-25T06:33:37.949808Z

Klaar, Sjoe. Beide MCP-problemen zijn gefixt en geverifieerd. Samenvatting:

WAT ER MIS WAS (twee losse dingen)

1. filesystem — config-bug: er stonden 5× letterlijk `--args` als argument in config.yaml, waardoor npm crashte met "Unknown cli flag: --args".

2. health-monitor — native module ABI-mismatch: de better-sqlite3 binary (genest in `mcp-server-health-monitor/node_modules/`) was gecompileerd voor Node 24, maar de gateway laadt MCP-servers met de Hermes-gebundelde Node 22. De binary uit 15 juni lag er nog.

WAT IK GEDAAN HEB

1. filesystem: `--args`-tokens verwijderd via `hermes config set`, allowlist-paden verbatim behouden (hermes-second-brain, Noa-Hermes, scripts, .hermes/skills) — conform je MCP-beveiligingsregel.

2. health-monitor: command van `node` naar absoluut pad `/usr/bin/node` gezet, omdat de bestaande binary exact voor Node 24 is gebouwd. Systeem-node v24 matcht perfect.

3. Gateway herstart + geverifieerd.

BEWIJS (bronnen)

- `hermes mcp list`: alle drie ✓ enabled (plex, health-monitor, filesystem)
- mcp-stderr.log na restart: health-monitor "Server started on stdio transport", filesystem "Secure MCP Filesystem Server running on stdio", plex "running on stdio"
- errors.log: geen "Connection closed" meer na de laatste restart (08:31)

Eén eerlijke kanttekening: de health-monitor draait nu op systeem-node v24 (bewust, want de binary is daarvoor gebouwd). Mocht je systeem-node ooit upgraden naar v25+, dan kan dit opnieuw breken — dan moet de binary gehercompileerd worden. Voor nu is alles groen.

{"success": true, "name": "evidence-ledger", "description": "Rigorous claim auditing methodology — track, label, and prove every assertion from Council analyses, backtests, and reports.", "tags": [], "related_skills": [], "content": "---\nname: evidence-ledger\ndescription: Rigorous claim auditing methodology — track, label, and prove every assertion from Council analyses, backtests, and reports.\n---\n\n# Evidence Ledger\n\nMethodology for auditing claims with traceable provenance, replicable evidence, and clear confidence labels.\n\n## When to use\n\n- A Council, analysis, or research output makes testable claims\n- A backtest or study produces WR/P&L/expectancy numbers\n- You need to separate PROVEN from ESTIMATE_ONLY before building anything\n- Lexi says \"bewijs het\" or \"waar komt dat vandaan?\"\n\n## Claim audit template\n\nEvery claim must document:\n\n1. **Claim** — exact percentage / WR / PF / expectancy\n2. **Bron** — welk bestand, welke agent, welke Council rol\n3. **Pad** — exact bestandspad indien aanwezig\n4. **Sample size** — aantal trades/events\n5. **Periode** — datumbereik\n6. **Pairs / timeframes** — welke markten\n7. **Getest of geschat?** — Ja/Nee\n8. **Oud of actueel?**\n9. **Label** — zie labels hieronder\n10. **Wat nog te bewijzen** — exacte volgende stap\n\n## Confidence labels\n\n| Label | Criteria |\n|-------|----------|\n| **PROVEN** | sample ≥ 300 trades, fees/slippage verwerkt, walk-forward/OOS aanwezig, reproduceerbaar command, output in bestand |\n| **PARTIAL** | goede sample (300+) maar fees ontbreken, of korte dataset, of geen OOS |\n| **OLD_SMALL_SAMPLE** | < 300 trades, of verouderde data, of geen fees |\n| **ESTIMATE_ONLY** | mondelinge schatting, 0 trades, geen code |\n| **REJECT_FOR_NOW** | bewezen fout of lookahead gevonden |\n\n## Analysis standards (from Lexi)\n\nEvery analysis must show:\n1. Minimal sample size\n2. Per-window replicatie (geen pooled-only)\n3. Baseline vergelijking\n4. Conditionele winrate (with/without)\n5. Median move\n6. Expectancy (na fees)\n7. Payoff ratio\n8. MFE/MAE\n9. Fees/slippage (indien trade-test)\n10. Unknown/missing-data uitgesloten uit rankings\n11. Reproduceerbaar command\n12. Outputbestand als bewijs\n\n## Verdict output format (from audit prompt pattern)\n\nWhen Lexi asks for a structured audit with pass/fail verdicts, use this output format.\nEvery claim must be backed by: literal code + line numbers + runtime output.\n\n### Structure\n\n```\nVERDICT: <exact label from allowed list>\nBEWIJS:\n  - Bestand: path/to/file.py regels XX-YY\n  - Code (letterlijk):\n    ```python\n    # de exacte code, gekopieerd uit read_file, niet geparafraseerd\n    ```\n  - Runtime output:\n    ```\n    $ python3 -c \"...\"\n    concrete output bewijs\n    ```\nWAT IS FOUT: <1-3 regels wat er technisch fout gaat>\nMINIMALE FIXRICHTING: <1-3 regels wat de fix zou zijn>\nGEEN COMMIT: <bevestiging dat er niks gewijzigd is>\n```\n\n### Allowed verdict labels\n\n| Prefix | Voorbeelden |\n|--------|-------------|\n| FAIL_ | FAIL_SOURCE_SWITCH, FAIL_RAW_GAPS, FAIL_RESAMPLE_ANCHOR, FAIL_RESAMPLE_OHLC, FAIL_EXTERNAL_TRUTH_MISMATCH, FAIL_RENDER_ONLY |\n| PASS_ | PASS_DATA_CONFIRMED |\n| INCONCLUSIVE_ | INCONCLUSIVE_EXTERNAL_TRUTH_MISSING |\n| REPAIR_ | REPAIR_APPLIED_VALIDATED, REPAIR_DRYRUN_ONLY, REPAIR_BLOCKED |\n| SOURCE_GUARD_ | SOURCE_GUARD_ADDED, SOURCE_GUARD_BLOCKED |\n\n### Requirements per verdict\n\nPASS_DATA_CONFIRMED mag alleen als:\n1. Raw candles compleet zijn\n2. OHLC exact uit raw candles klopt\n3. External truth matcht\n4. Geen source switch/gap/fill probleem\n5. Candle size statistiek verklaarbaar is vanuit raw truth\n\n### Evidence requirements\n\n- GEEN parafrase -- letterlijke code uit read_file()\n- GEEN conclusie zonder runtime output\n- Runtime output = echt commando + echte output, niet \"zou moeten werken\"\n- KAN NIET VERIFIEREN = acceptabel verdict als bewijs ontbreekt, maar zeg WAAROM\n\n## Entry-Edge vs Exit-Edge Diagnostic\n\n**Scheid ALTIJD entry-edge van exit-edge.** Dit is de belangrijkste les uit de winner-archetype analyse.\n\n### Waarom?\n\nEen strategie kan 60% exit WR tonen maar slechts 40% entry hit rate (exit redt slechte entries).\nOmgekeerd: 45% exit WR met 70% entry hit rate (entry werkt, exit vernietigt).\n\nZonder deze scheiding kan je niet zien of je de entry of de exit moet verbeteren.\n\n### Hoe meten?\n\n**Entry-edge** = directional accuracy op fixed horizon na entry:\n```\nhit_rate_5  = % trades waar prijs na 5 candles in juiste richting beweegt\nhit_rate_10 = % trades waar prijs na 10 candles in juiste richting beweegt\nhit_rate_20 = % trades waar prijs na 20 candles in juiste richting beweegt\n```\n\n**Exit-edge** = WR van het SL/TP/trailing systeem:\n```\nexit_wr     = WIN / (WIN + LOSS) volgens exit logica\npayoff      = gem_win / gem_loss\nmfe_mae_ratio = MFE / |MAE|\n```\n\n### Interpretatie\n\n| Patroon | Betekenis | Actie |\n|---------|-----------|-------|\n| Hit10 > exit_wr + 10pp | Entry werkt, exit vernietigt | Fix exit, niet entry |\n| Hit10 < exit_wr - 10pp | Exit redt slechte entries | Fix entry, niet exit |\n| Hit10 ≈ exit_wr | Entry en exit matchen | Beide verbeteren of nieuw idee |\n| MFE/MAE > 1.5 maar payoff < 0.5 | Exit knipt winsten te vroeg af | Trailing/TP te strak |\n| MFE/MAE < 0.5 | Entry heeft geen intrinsieke edge | Geen exit fix gaat helpen |\n\n### Praktijkvoorbeeld (downtrend + near_resistance)\n\n```\nHit10 = 72.2%  ← entry werkt\nMFE/MAE = 2.73 ← entry heeft intrinsieke upside\nExit WR = 11.1% ← exit vernietigt ALLE waarde\nPayoff = 0.15  ← verliezen 6.7x groter dan winsten\n```\n\nConclusie: entry is de parel, exit is het lijk. Geen entry-aanpassingen doen — enkel exit fixen.\n\n### Exit replay protocol\n\nWanneer exit-edge zwak is maar entry-edge sterk:\n\n1. Herhaal de trade met exacte SL/TP/trailing logica\n2. Log exit_reason (stop_loss / take_profit / trailing_stop / time_exit / end_of_data)\n3. Bereken: time_to_MFE, time_to_MAE, bars_to_MFE, bars_to_MAE\n4. Test fixed horizon exits (1/3/5/10/20 candles) als diagnostiek\n5. Test partial take-profit (bijv. 50% op +0.6%, 50% trailing)\n6. Rapporteer ALLE varianten apart — nooit samensmelten\n\n## Hermes context rule\n\nALLE Hermes contextlagen (L2-L9) worden standaard meegenomen in elk rapport.\nElke contextlaag moet historisch/as-of berekend worden zonder lookahead.\nGeen actuele dashboard/director context als bewijs.\n\n## Layer 99: Fullstack Evidence Layer\n\nCombineert ALLE bestaande Hermes-lagen (L2-L8) met trade-outcome-data in één auditbaar rapport per trade.\n\n### Doel\n\nGeen predictor. Geen strategie. Geen trade-advies. Alleen bewijzen wat er gebeurde.\n\n### Per trade vastleggen (read-only)\n\n| Laag | Data | Hoe importeren |\n|------|------|----------------|\n| L1 | candle open/high/low/close/volume | Uit OHLC data |\n| L2 | swing highs/lows, afstand tot laatste swing | `from fractals import vind_fractalen, _scheid_toppen_bodems` |\n| L3 | phase (D/U/R), compression | `label_phases(pts, interval_minutes)` — runnen vanuit `layer3_phase/` dir |\n| L4 | trendlines | Via `chart_engine.build_chart()` of directe trendline import |\n| L5 | cockpit | Nog niet geïntegreerd in Layer 99 |\n| L6 | micro state, body trend, wick bias, consec counts | `from candle_micro import analyze_candle_micro` |\n| L7 | EMA regime, ATR/volatility, MA cross | `from indicator_context import read_indicator_context_from_candles(pair, tf, candles, lookback=N)` — **let op: functienaam is `_from_candles`** |\n| L8 | market wind, BTC direction, alignment | `from market_context import read_market_context_from_candles(pair, timeframe, pair_candles, btc_candles, eth_candles)` |\n\n### Entry timing labels\n\n| Label | Betekenis |\n|-------|-----------|\n| near_reversal | Entry ≤1 candle na swing high/low |\n| late | Entry 2-3 candles na swing |\n| chase_entry | Entry 4-6 candles na swing (achter feiten aan) |\n| mid_range | Entry midden in range, geen duidelijke reversal |\n| not_controllable | Te weinig data |\n\n### Exit timing labels\n\n| Label | Betekenis |\n|-------|-----------|\n| early | TP geraakt, exit voor de top |\n| late | End-of-data of te laat uitgestapt |\n| gave_back_profit | Trailing stop gaf winst terug |\n| invalidation_missed | SL niet gerespecteerd of te wijd |\n| not_controllable | Onbekend |\n\n### Final verdict\n\n| Label | Betekenis |\n|-------|-----------|\n| win | Trade positief afgesloten (let op: kan nog steeds slechte timing hebben) |\n| exit_failed | Entry ok maar exit fout |\n| management_failed | Trailing/management fout |\n| context_failed | Hermes context voorspelde niks nuttigs |\n| data_missing | Te weinig data voor conclusie |\n| not_controllable | Onbekend |\n\n### Output\n    \n- CSV: per trade één rij met alle lagen + timing labels\n- JSON: per trade als dict\n- Markdown: rapport met per-laag samenvatting\n\n### Timestamp semantics — verplichte diagnose vóór elke chart-generatie\n\n**Voordat je Layer 98 charts genereert of Layer 99 semantiek interpreteert, bewijs eerst welke candle wat is.**\n\nDe grootste fout: aannemen dat `candle_entry` de entry-candle is. Dit is vaak de SIGNAL candle.\n\n#### Diagnose-stappen\n\n1. **Lees de source CSV** — check of `entry_ts` en `signal_ts` bestaan\n2. **Trace `entry_idx`** in de code:\n   ```python\n   entry_idx = next(j for j,c in enumerate(candles) if c['timestamp'] >= entry_ts) - 1\n   ```\n   Dit geeft de candle VOOR entry_ts (= signal candle)\n3. **Vergelijk timestamps:**\n   - `candle_entry.ts + 900 == entry_ts` → candle_entry = SIGNAL candle\n   - `candle_after_1.ts == entry_ts` → candle_after_1 = ACTUAL ENTRY candle\n\n#### Correcte labeling\n\n| Veld | Moet zijn |\n|------|-----------|\n| `candle_entry.ts` | De candle waar entry daadwerkelijk opened (entry execution) |\n| `candle_after_1.ts` | DE candle NA entry (1ste volledige candle in de trade) |\n| `candle_entry` rol | ACTUAL_ENTRY_CANDLE (niet SIGNAL_CANDLE) |\n\n#### Waarom dit ertoe doet\n\nEen chart met `candle_entry` als signal candle en `candle_after_1` als entry candle betekent:\n- Entry marker staat op de verkeerde candle\n- After_1 return meet vanaf entry candle ipv erna\n- Exit timing misrekend\n\n#### Debug charts\n\nMaak bij twijfel een debug chart met 4 verticale lijnen:\n1. `CANDLE_ENTRY_FIELD` — wat Layer 99 nu als `candle_entry` labelt\n2. `ACTUAL_ENTRY_TS` — de echte `entry_ts` uit de trade data\n3. `CANDLE_AFTER_1_FIELD` — wat Layer 99 nu als `candle_after_1` labelt\n4. `ACTUAL_EXIT_TS` — de echte `exit_ts`\n\n### Belangrijke valkuilen\n\n- **Functienamen verschillen per laag.** L7 heeft `read_indicator_context_from_candles` (niet `read_indicator_context`). L8 heeft `read_market_context_from_candles` (niet `read_market_context`). Check ALTIJD de functiesignatuur.\n- **L3 heeft relatieve imports.** Moet runnen vanuit `layer3_phase/` directory of subprocess gebruiken.\n- **L7 closed-candle policy** sluit laatste candle uit. Gebruik `lookback=N` parameter om voldoende data te geven.\n- **L7 ma_cross key heet `direction`**, niet `state`. Waarden: `none`, `bullish`, `bearish`.\n- **L7 atr key** zit in `result['atr']['volatility_state']` en `result['atr']['atr_pct']`.\n- **L7 ma_regime** zit in `result['ma_regime']['regime']`.\n- **L8** verwacht `(pair, timeframe, pair_candles, btc_candles, eth_candles)` — eth_candles=None als niet beschikbaar.\n- **L8 quality is vaak `warning`** in historische context. Dat is normaal — betekent dat L8 minder benchmarkdata heeft dan live. Niet negeren, maar ook niet als fout behandelen. Documenteer in rapport als `present_with_warning`.\n- **Exit timing labels zijn mappings, geen metingen.** `stop_loss → invalidation_missed`, `trailing_stop → gave_back_profit`, `take_profit → early`, `end_of_data → late`. Dit zijn exit-reason vertalingen, geen onafhankelijke metingen. Rapporteer als: `exit_timing_label_source = exit_reason_mapping`.\n- **Entry timing is een benadering** gebaseerd op candles sinds laatste swing high. Exactheid hangt af van swing-detectie parameters (n=2 in fractals). Documenteer als: `entry_timing_source = bars_since_swing_high_via_fractal_n2`.\n\n## OOS Walk-Forward Protocol\n\n### Wanneer gebruiken\n\nNa archetype mining of winner-patroon detectie — om te bewijzen dat het patroon buiten de gevonden sample blijft werken.\n\n### Stappen\n\n1. **Split data in mining-sample en OOS-sample**\n   - Mining: de periode waarin het patroon ontdekt werd\n   - OOS: een andere, niet-gebruikte periode (bv. vorig jaar, volgende maand)\n\n2. **Walk-forward windows**\n   - 12+ windows van ~1 maand\n   - Per window apart rapporteren (niet poolen)\n   - Window schuift elke week/maand\n\n3. **Per window meten**\n   - Trades, WR, expectancy, payoff\n   - Hit rates op 1/3/5/10/20 candles\n   - MFE, MAE, MFE/MAE ratio\n   - Vergelijk met baseline (alle trades in die window)\n\n4. **Kill criteria**\n   - n < 100 totaal → onvoldoende\n   - Edge in ≤3 windows → UNSTABLE\n   - Net PF < 1.0 → REJECT\n   - Net expectancy ≤ 0 → REJECT\n   - Max DD < -15% → REJECT\n\n5. **Rapporteer**\n   - Mining resultaten (ontdekkings-sample)\n   - OOS resultaten (verificatie-sample)\n   - Baseline vergelijking\n   - Window-stabiliteit\n\n### Labels\n\n| Label | Criteria |\n|-------|----------|\n| OOS_CANDIDATE | Hit10 ≥ 55% + MFE/MAE ≥ 1.2 + n ≥ 15 OOS |\n| INCONCLUSIVE | Hit10 ≥ 50% + n ≥ 10 OOS |\n| REJECT | Patroon herhaalt niet in OOS |\n\n## Winner Archetype Mining\n\n### Doel\n\nVan een set trades met losers EN winners: zoek welke Hermes-context het verschil maakt. Geen simulator, geen predictor — alleen contrastive pattern mining.\n\n### Stappen\n\n1. **Split trades**\n   - WINNERS vs LOSERS\n   - BIG_WINNERS (top 25%) vs BIG_LOSERS (bottom 25%)\n\n2. **Per trade: Hermes context as-of**\n   - L2: swing highs/lows, afstand\n   - L3: phase/compression\n   - L4: near_resistance/near_support/middle\n   - L6: candle micro/wick/body\n   - L7: EMA regime, ATR/volatility, MA cross\n   - L8: BTC direction/market wind\n\n3. **Contrastive analysis**\n   - P(value | winner) vs P(value | loser)\n   - enrichment_ratio\n   - win_rate_when_value_present vs win_rate_when_value_absent\n   - avg_net_return en median_net_return\n\n4. **Anti-overfit regels**\n   - n < 20 → SKIP\n   - Slechts 1 window → SKIP\n   - expectancy ≤ 0 → SKIP\n   - payoff_ratio < 1 → SKIP\n   - Unknown/missing context als signaal → SKIP\n\n5. **Output**\n   - Enrichment CSV: per conditie/kenmerk\n   - Archetype CSV: per combinatie\n   - Markdown rapport met top kandidaten + anti-overfit check\n\n## Standards for Hermes Layer Function Calls\n\n### Import patterns\n\n```python\n# ALTIJD de _from_candles variant gebruiken voor historische data\n# L6\nfrom candle_micro import analyze_candle_micro\nl6 = analyze_candle_micro(candles, lookback=5, pair=pair, timeframe=tf)\n\n# L7 — NIET read_indicator_context gebruiken (die fetch Kraken)\nfrom indicator_context import read_indicator_context_from_candles\nl7 = read_indicator_context_from_candles(pair, tf, candles, lookback=30)\n\n# L8 — NIET read_market_context gebruiken (die fetch Kraken)\nfrom market_context import read_market_context_from_candles\nl8 = read_market_context_from_candles(pair, 15, pair_candles, btc_candles, eth_candles)\n```\n\n### L4 trendline integration (read-only)\n\nL4 functies (`select_upper_points`, `select_lower_points`, `_validate_candidate`) verwachten Fractal-objecten met een `strength` attribuut. Hermes L2 fractals hebben dat niet — ze hebben alleen `index`, `prijs`, `type`.\n\n**Fix:** wrap L2 Fractals in een lokale klasse die `strength` toevoegt. Geen L4 code aanpassen.\n\n```python\nclass L4Fractal:\n    def __init__(self, idx, prijs, typ):\n        self.index = idx\n        self.prijs = prijs\n        self.type = typ\n        self.strength = 0  # L4 verwacht dit, L2 geeft het niet\n\n# Van L2 fractals naar L4 formaat\ntops, bodems = _scheid_toppen_bodems(vind_fractalen(candles, n=2))\nft = [L4Fractal(f.index, f.prijs, f.type) for f in tops]\nfb = [L4Fractal(f.index, f.prijs, f.type) for f in bodems]\n\nup_pts = select_upper_points(ft, candles, max_points=15)\nlo_pts = select_lower_points(fb, candles, max_points=15)\nup_cands = generate_upper_candidates(up_pts)\ntop_cand = _pick_top(up_cands)\nvalid = _validate_candidate(top_cand, candles, up_pts, 'high', interval_minutes, is_upper=True)\n```\n\n### Key names per laag\n\n| Laag | Return structuur | Let op! |\n|------|-----------------|---------|\n| L6 | `result['summary']['micro_state']`, `['body_trend']`, `['wick_bias']`, `['consecutive_bullish']`, `['consecutive_bearish']` | |\n| L7 | `result['ma_regime']['regime']`, `['ma_cross']['direction']`, `['atr']['volatility_state']`, `['atr']['atr_pct']` | **`ma_cross` gebruikt `direction` (bullish/bearish/none), NIET `state`.** `bars_since` kan None zijn. |\n| L8 | `result['market_wind']`, `['btc_direction']`, `['pair_direction']`, `['direction_alignment']`, `['relative_behavior']` | |\n\n### Import pitfalls\n\n| Probleem | Fix |\n|----------|-----|\n| L3/L4 import faalt: `from .layer3_config import ...` of `from .fractals import ...` | Punt weghalen: `from layer3_config import ...` — het geïmporteerde bestand heeft zelf geen relatieve imports |\n| L3 `label_phases()` geeft onverwachte labels | `label_phases()` retourneert `'D'`, `'U'`, `'R'` in `phase_labels[-1]['final_label']`, niet de strings `\"downtrend\"`/`\"uptrend\"`. **Mapping bug trap:** `if 'downtrend' in label` matcht nooit en valt altijd naar `else → R`. Gebruik `if label == 'D'` in plaats van substring matching. |\n| L7 functie gevonden maar verkeerde naam | Gebruik `read_indicator_context_from_candles`, NIET `read_indicator_context` |\n| L7 closed-candle policy sluit laatste candle uit | Geef minstens `lookback+1` candles. Default lookback=200. Voor kleine datasets: `lookback=30` |\n| L7 outcome is leeg/UNKNOWN | Check key namen — `ma_cross` heeft `direction`, niet `state` |\n| L8 `read_market_context_from_candles` faalt | Check volgorde: `(pair, timeframe, pair_candles, btc_candles, eth_candles)`. eth_candles mag None. |\n| L8 `read_market_context` zonder `_from_candles` | Die variante fetch Kraken live data — NIET gebruiken voor historische analyse |\n\n## Layer 98: Historical Chart Generation\n\n### Harde regel: GEBRUIK ALTIJD V5\n\n**NOOIT een eigen matplotlib renderer bouwen voor marktcontext.** De V5 renderer (`layer5_cockpit/structure_cockpit.py`) tekent alle marktcontext (candles, fractals, S/R, trendlines, L3 labels, L4 context). Jouw taak is alleen: lokale candles doorgeven aan V5 + viewport overschrijven op lokale prijsrange + trade overlays toevoegen.\n\n**Waarom?** Zonder V5 mist de chart: fractals/swing markers, S/R zones, trendlines, L3 labels, L4 context. Lexi heeft dit meerdere keren gecorrigeerd (\"is dat nu zo fucking moeilijk om layer 5 te kopiëren\").\n\n**Werkwijze:**\n```python\n# 1. Laad lokale candles (48 vóór entry, 32 erna)\n# 2. Roep V5 _render_single_tf() aan met candles_override\n# 3. Overschrijf y-axis op lokale prijsrange (forceer set_ylim)\n# 4. Voeg entry marker, resistance zone, SHORT_ENTRY_TEST label toe\n# 5. Voeg context box toe met L5/L6/L7 data\n# 6. Schrijf sidecar JSON\n```\n\nZie `references/full-context-chart-standard.md` voor de volledige standaard mét L5/L6/L7 verplichtingen, sidecar JSON schema, HTF filter regels en render audit.\n\n### Workflow (fallback — alleen als V5 niet beschikbaar is)\n\n1. Laad historische OHLC data uit CSV/JSONL\n2. Neem een slice van 40-80 candles rond de trade (20 voor signaal, 20+ erna)\n3. RoeP `build_chart()` aan met die slice — **geen PIL overlays, geen eigen matplotlib**\n4. Serveer de gegenereerde PNGs via een HTTP server\n\n### Chart varianten per trade\n\n| Variant | Candle slice | Doel |\n|---------|-------------|------|\n| `asof_entry` | 80 voor tot 5 na entry | Pre-entry context (Hermes lagen op signaalmoment) |\n| `asof_exit` | 80 voor tot 5 na exit | Exit context (wat zag de chart bij exit?) |\n| `outcome_full` | 5 voor entry tot 12 na exit | Volledig trade verloop |\n| `entry_plus_10` | 3 voor tot 12 na entry | Korte-termijn price action na entry |\n\n### Regels\n\n- Gebruik ALTIJD `build_chart()` met `show_swings=True, show_major_trend=True, show_sr_zones=True, show_pivot_rays=True`\n- Geen PIL/OpenCV overlays — die aligneren niet met matplotlib rendering\n- Chart link in evidence record: absoluut pad of HTTP URL\n- Als chart niet gegenereerd: `VERWIJDERD` label, niet leeg laten\n\n### Chart rendering regels (uit correction prompt)\n\n1. **ASOF vs OUTCOME streng scheiden.** ASOF gebruikt alleen candles tot signal/entry cutoff. OUTCOME gebruikt replay-window inclusief post-entry/post-exit candles. Voeg een guard toe die faalt als ASOF candles bevat na entry/exit cutoff.\n2. **Viewport gebaseerd op auditrange**, niet op V5-objecten. Bepaal `price_min` en `price_max` uit candles + entry/exit/SL/TP. Voeg 5-8% padding toe. V5-lijnen die ver buiten deze range vallen mogen geclipt worden of niet meegenomen in autoscale.\n3. **TP/SL als duidelijke doorlopende lijnen.** SL-lijn loopt minstens van entry-index tot einde zichtbare window. TP-lijn idem. Lijnen mogen niet verdwijnen achter V5-overlay. Labels rechts van de lijn plaatsen, niet midden op candles.\n4. **SIGNAL-label gekoppeld aan signal candle.** Verticale marker aan onderkant van de chart, niet los zwevend bovenaan. Compacte marker net onder de candle.\n5. **Label collision vermijden.** Simpele offset: als labels dicht bij elkaar liggen, verschuif ze verticaal. TP/SL rechts van de chart plaatsen.\n6. **Post-exit candles tellen.** OUTCOME chart toont minstens 5 candles na exit. Map `post_exit_candle_count` in audit metadata. Als minder dan 5 beschikbaar: toon wat er is, label in infobox.\n7. **Geen stille failures.** Log per chart: trade_id, mode, visible_start/end, candle count, post_exit count, y_min/max, aantal V5-objecten zichtbaar versus geclipt.\n\n### V5 Replay Adapter (aanbevolen)\n\nGebruik de V5 historical replay adapter voor trade-audit charts. Dit is beter dan losse `build_chart()` calls omdat V5 de volledige marktcontext tekent (S/R, trendlines, L3, L4, L4a).\n\nZie `references/v5-historical-replay-adapter.md` voor de volledige implementatie.\n\n### Voorbeeld (V5 replay)\n\n```python\nfrom layer98_historical_replay.historical_v5_replay_adapter import render_historical_trade_chart\n\ntrade_info = {\n    'pair': 'ETHEUR', 'side': 'short', 'window': 'w1',\n    'entry_price': 2064.71, 'exit_price': 2053.065,\n    'signal_ts': 1706094000, 'entry_ts': 1706094900, 'exit_ts': 1706111100,\n    'exit_reason': Discovery\n\n**`build_validation_snapshot_from_candles()` in `layer9_validation_lab/validation_lab.py:149` is de dichtstbijzijnde bestaande centrale contextlaag.**\n\nDeze functie combineert:\n- L6 (candle micro)\n- L7 (indicatoren via `read_indicator_context_from_candles`)\n- L8 (market context)\n- Future outcomes (next_3/5/10/20 candles)\n- Strikte as-of scheiding via `candles[:snapshot_index+1]` vs `candles[snapshot_index+1:]`\n\nHet is een PURE functie — geen IO, geen Kraken fetch.\n\n```python\nresult = build_validation_snapshot_from_candles(\n    pair, timeframe, pair_candles, btc_candles, eth_candles,\n    snapshot_index, future_windows=(3,5,10,20)\n)\n# result['layers'] = {'l6_micro': ..., 'l7_indicator': ..., 'l8_market_context': ...}\n# afstand niet structuur-gebaseerd (3/18) |\n| EXIT_END_OF_DATA | Trade niet gesloten binnen window (4/18) |\n| EXIT_UNCLEAR | Onbekend |\n\n### MFE Capture Quality\n\n| Quality | Criteria | Voorkomen (18 trades) |\n|---------|----------|----------------------|\n| GOOD_CAPTURE | PnL ≥ 70% van MFE | 3/18 |\n| PARTIAL_CAPTURE | PnL 30-70% van MFE | 1/18 |\n| BAD_CAPTURE | PnL < 30% van MFE | **14/18** |\n| NO_MFE | MFE = 0 | 0/18 |\n\n### Praktijkvoorbeeld: downtrend + near_resistance (18 trades)\n\n```\nEntry: 16/18 mid_range (te laat), 1/18 chase, 1/18 against structure\nExit:  5/18 Vergelijk executed trades (de 18) met alle kandidaten\n\n### Kandidaat detectie (downtrend + near_resistance)\n\n```python\ndef detect_candidates(candles, lookback=80):\n    for i in range(lookback, len(candles)-5):\n        slice = candles[max(0,i-lookback):i+1]\n        f = vind_fractalen(slice, n=2)\n        tops, bodems = _scheid_toppen_bodems(f)\n        if len(tops) < 2 or len(bodems) < 2: continue\n        \n        h2, h1 = tops[-2].prijs, tops[-1].prijs\n        l2, l1 = bodems[-2].prijs, bodems[-1].prijs\n        downtrend = h1 < h2 and l1 < l2\n        \n        rng_pct = (h1 - slice[-1].close) / (h1 - l1) * 100 if h1 > l1 else 100\n        near_res = rng_pct < 20\n        \n        if downtrend and near_res:\n            candidates.append(...)\n```\n\n### Exit replay voor kandidaten\n\nGebruik exact dezelfde SL/TP/trailing logica als legacy momentum:\n- SL = swing_high + 0.5×ATR (short)\n- TP = entry - (SL - entry) × 2.5\n- Trailing start na 1:1 RR\n\n### Vergelijkingsdata\n\n| Group | n | WR | avg PnL | avg MFE | avg MAE |\n|-------|---|----|---------|---------|---------|\n| executed | 18 | — | — | — | — |\n| all candidates | variabel | — | — | — | — |\n| skipped | executed — candidates_in_common | — | — | — | — |\n\nVerdict mogelijke waarden: SELECTION_PROBLEM, EXIT_PROBLEM, BOTH, EXECUTED_BETTER, NOT_ENOUGH_DATA\n\n## Candidate Context Snapshot Schema\n\nConceptueel minimum-record voor één kandidaat/trade:\n\n```\ncandidate_context_snapshot:\n  record_id, candidate_id, pair, timeframe, side, candidate_ts\n  \n  asof_context:      # Only candles + context up to candidate_ts\n    candle_window, L2, L3, L4, S/R, L6, L7, L8\n  \n  decision_context:   # Why candidate? {"content": "1|\"\"\"\n2|Outcome Builder — Window Calculator\n3|\n4|Computes outcome windows from OHLC candles.\n5|Inclusive start (>= asof), exclusive end (< asof + window).\n6|Strict status: complete/partial/missing.\n7|\"\"\"\n8|\n9|from typing import Any\n10|\n11|from .contracts import ALLOWED_WINDOWS\n12|\n13|\n14|def compute_windows(\n15|    asof_ts: int,\n16|    reference_price: float,\n17|    candles: list[dict],\n18|    windows: dict[str, int],\n19|    asof_on_boundary: bool,\n20|) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:\n21|    \"\"\"\n22|    Compute outcome windows from candles.\n23|\n24|    Args:\n25|        asof_ts: Snapshot asof timestamp.\n26|        reference_price: Reference price from snapshot.\n27|        candles: List of candle dicts with timestamp, open, high, low, close.\n28|        windows: {name: seconds} dict.\n29|        asof_on_boundary: Whether asof is on 1m boundary.\n30|\n31|    Returns:\n32|        Dict of window name -> outcome data.\n33|    \"\"\"\n34|    results = {}\n35|    timestamps = [c[\"timestamp\"] for c in candles]\n36|\n37|    for win_name, win_seconds in windows.items():\n38|        window_start = asof_ts\n39|        window_end = asof_ts + win_seconds\n40|\n41|        # Filter candles: timestamp >= start AND timestamp < end\n42|        included = [\n43|            c for c in candles\n44|            if c[\"timestamp\"] >= window_start and c[\"timestamp\"] < window_end\n45|        ]\n46|\n47|        expected = win_seconds // 60  # 1m candles\n48|        found = len(included)\n49|\n50|        # Status\n51|        if found == expected:\n52|            status = \"complete\"\n53|        elif found == 0:\n54|            status = \"missing\"\n55|        else:\n56|            status = \"partial\"\n57|\n58|        # Compute fields\n59|        if found > 0:\n60|            final_candle = included[-1]\n61|            final_close = final_candle[\"close\"]\n62|\n63|            # high and low\n64|            high_val = max(c[\"high\"] for c in included)\n65|            low_val = min(c[\"low\"] for c in included)\n66|\n67|            # Find first occurrence of high and low\n68|            high_candle = next(c for c in included if c[\"high\"] == high_val)\n69|            low_candle = next(c for c in included if c[\"low\"] == low_val)\n70|            high_ts = high_candle[\"timestamp\"]\n71|            low_ts = low_candle[\"timestamp\"]\n72|\n73|            # Deltas\n74|            close_delta_abs = final_close - reference_price\n75|            close_delta_pct = (close_delta_abs / reference_price) * 100\n76|            max_up_abs = high_val - reference_price\n77|            max_up_pct = (max_up_abs / reference_price) * 100\n78|            # max_down = positive magnitude of downside move\n79|            max_down_abs = max(0.0, reference_price - low_val)\n80|            max_down_pct = (max_down_abs / reference_price) * 100\n81|        else:\n82|            final_close = None\n83|            high_val = None\n84|            high_ts = None\n85|            low_val = None\n86|            low_ts = None\n87|            close_delta_abs = None\n88|            close_delta_pct = None\n89|            max_up_abs = None\n90|            max_up_pct = None\n91|            max_down_abs = None\n92|            max_down_pct = None\n93|\n94|        results[win_name] = {\n95|            \"status\": status,\n96|            \"window_start_ts\": window_start,\n97|            \"window_end_ts\": window_end,\n98|            \"candles_expected\": expected,\n99|            \"candles_found\": found,\n100|            \"final_close\": final_close,\n101|            \"high\": high_val,\n102|            \"high_ts\": high_ts,\n103|            \"low\": low_val,\n104|            \"low_ts\": low_ts,\n105|            \"close_delta_abs\": close_delta_abs,\n106|            \"close_delta_pct\": close_delta_pct,\n107|            \"max_up_abs\": max_up_abs,\n108|            \"max_up_pct\": max_up_pct,\n109|            \"max_down_abs\": max_down_abs,\n110|            \"max_down_pct\": max_down_pct,\n111|        }\n112|\n113|    return results\n114|", "total_lines": 113, "file_size": 3548, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

Niet een trading-profitability engine.\n7|\n8|We meten, bovenop de bevroren historische execution chain, of een strategiebeslissing\n9|(LONG/SHORT/NO_SIGNAL) achteraf een prijsbeweging in de gunstige richting zag —\n10|via de frozen Outcome die puur beschrijvend meet wat de prijs ná dat moment deed.\n11|\n12|## Waarom?\n13|Phase3B kan nu betrouwbaar dezelfde historische strategy-decisions reproduceren.\n14|Maar we hebben nog geen bevroren definitie waarmee die decisions eerlijk beoordeeld\n15|worden. Zonder die definitie zouden we de meetlat achteraf kunnen aanpassen aan\n16|wat er toevallig goed uitkomt. Eerst de meetlat vastleggen, dan pas kijken.\n17|\n18|## Waar staan we nu?\n19|Phase 0 — contract in opmaak. Discovery en gap-audit zijn afgerond. Er is nog\n20|niets geïmplementeerd, geen enkele strategie is gescoord.\n21|\n22|## Wat kan het al?\n23|Dit contract zelf: niets. De onderliggende keten wel: snapshot → frozen provider\n24|→ StrategyInput v2 → decision (NO_SIGNAL/LONG/SHORT) → frozen Outcome\n25|(5m/15m/60m/240m, close_delta, max_up, max_down, compleetheid) → deterministische\n26|Batch-v2 replay. Alles bevroren en getest (core 325/325, real-data 39/39,\n27|Foundation 951/951 ×2).\n28|\n29|## Wat kan het nog niet?\n30|- echte PnL / winst-verlies\n31|- Sharpe / expectancy / drawdown\n32|- portfolio performance\n33|- optimizer / parameter search\n34|- strategy ranking / promotie\n35|- betrouwbare statistische-zekerheidsclaims\n36|\n37|## Wat is de blocker?\n38|Geen. De contract kan geschreven worden en is review-ready.\n39|\n40|## Wat is de volgende stap?\n41|Onafhankelijke review van dit contract. Daarna pas implementatie (Phase 4A).\n42|\n43|## Wanneer is Phase 0 klaar?\n44|Wanneer dit contract onafhankelijk gereviewed en bevroren is, en er dus een exacte,\n45|getekende definitie ligt van wat gemeten mag worden, welke Outcome-data gebruikt\n46|mag worden, hoe LONG/SHORT genormaliseerd worden, hoe NO_SIGNAL behandeld wordt,\n47|hoe compleetheid gerapporteerd wordt, welke claims verboden zijn, en welke evidence\n48|nog onvoldoende is.\n49|\n50|## Wat is het einddoel?\n51|Een scorecard die aantoont of een strategie een signaal produceert dat beter is dan\n52|toeval — zonder cherry-picking, zonder fake PnL, zonder achteraf de lat te verleggen —\n53|vóór er ook maar één euro live riskeert te gaan.\n54|\n55|De claim \"beter dan toeval\" mag alleen gemaakt worden ná de nog te bevroren\n56|baseline/negative-control gate (CONTRACT.md §23); zonder die gate blijft dit een\n57|beschrijvende scorecard, geen predictive-value claim.\n58|\n59|# Engineering Layer\n60|\n61|## Frozen base\n62|Frozen Phase3B freeze commit: 213d77dbc8218e5d061ee641376cbec07f98724d\n63|Frozen branch: frozen/strategy-harness-phase3b-batch-v2-historical-replay-20260818\n64|Tag: strategy-harness-phase3b-batch-v2-historical-replay-frozen-20260819\n65|RC4 GREEN review: 5977456f07763387f2f1ea3a57bbdd81d5ba3c94\n66|\n67|## Current phase\n68|Strategy Evaluation — Contract Phase 0 (docs only)\n69|\n70|## Implementation\n71|none\n72|\n73|## Strategy scores viewed\n74|no\n75|\n76|## Open decisions\n77|- minimum sample-size N (geen onderbouwde drempel)\n78|- correlated-snapshot statistische afhankelijkheid\n79|- concrete percentile-set\n80|- reward/risk asymmetry formule\n81|- statistical uncertainty (CI/bootstrap)\n82|\n83|## Next\n84|independent contract review\n85|", "total_lines": 84, "file_size": 3212, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

Ik heb nu het volledige frozen contract + de volledige Phase1A interface + de Outcome calculator/store gelezen. Hier is het design-rapport:

RAPPORTEER UITSLUITEND

STATUS:
READY_TO_IMPLEMENT_PRIMITIVES

HUMAN_SUMMARY:
Phase1B legt bovenop de bevroren Phase1A-join de eerste échte meetlat neer: per strategiebeslissing (LONG/SHORT/NO_SIGNAL) meten we, per muntpaar en per vooraf vastgelegde horizon (5m/15m/60m/240m), of de prijs achteraf in de gunstige richting bewoog (richting) en hoever de gunstige/ongunstige uitslag ging (excursie). Na deze fase kan NOA-Reign dus antwoorden: "hoe vaak signaleert deze strategie" (coverage), "hoe vaak zat de richting goed/mis/vlak" (hit/miss/flat), en "wat was de gemiddelde gunstige en ongunstige prijsbeweging" (excursie-samenvattingen) — alles descriptief, alles apart per paar/richting/horizon. Dit is nog steeds GEEN trading-winst: er is geen entry/exit/execution/risk/fees-contract, dus er bestaat hier geen PnL, geen Sharpe, geen expectancy. We bouwen bewust geen één master-score, want één getal kan een slechte LONG-richting of een slecht paar verbergen — de scorecard blijft altijd uit componenten bestaan. LONG en SHORT blijven apart omdat een gunstige beweging voor een LONG (prijs omhoog) precies omgekeerd is voor een SHORT (prijs omlaag); samenvoegen zou betekenisloos zijn. Elke horizon blijft apart omdat een signaal dat op 5m werkt niks zegt over 240m. NO_SIGNAL hoort alleen bij coverage (hoe actief de strategie is), niet bij signaalkwaliteit (hoe goed de actieve signalen waren) — een "afzijdig blijven" heeft geen gunstige of ongunstige richting om te scoren, en we mogen geen achteraf-"goed afzijdig gebleven"-bonus verzinnen. Bewust onbeantwoord blijft: wat is een minimale steekproefgrootte, zijn de samples statistisch onafhankelijk, welke extra percentielen (p10/p25/…) willen we, en is er een reward/risk-ratio — die blijven open tot er bewijs is.

OUTCOME_FIELDS_USABLE:
per horizon (5m/15m/60m/240m) uit Outcome windows_data: status{complete|partial|missing}, candles_expected, candles_found, close_delta_pct, max_up_pct, max_down_pct, plus provenance (final_close, high, low, high_ts, low_ts, close_delta_abs, max_up_abs, max_down_abs, window_start_ts, window_end_ts). Identiteit: outcome_id, record_id, record_revision, windows_hash, pair, snapshot_id, asof_ts.

METRICS_IN_SCOPE:
counts (OBSERVATIONS_TOTAL, ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS_TOTAL, LONG_COUNT, SHORT_COUNT, NO_SIGNAL_COUNT); coverage ratio; per-horizon completeness (EXPECTED/OUTCOME_AVAILABLE/COMPLETE/PARTIAL/MISSING/EXCLUDED); directional HIT/MISS/FLAT + hit-rate (per pair/direction/horizon); favorable excursion COUNT/MEAN/MEDIAN; adverse excursion COUNT/MEAN/MEDIAN; breakdowns (pair, direction, horizon); exclusion reason-code tallies; EVIDENCE_STATUS.

METRICS_DEFERRED:
composite score; reward/risk ratio; tail-risk; Sharpe; expectancy; drawdown; profit factor; PnL; baseline delta; statistical confidence/CI; additional percentile set (p10/p25/p75/p90/p95/p99); multiple-testing correction engine; optimizer/ranking.

NO_SIGNAL_POLICY:
NO_SIGNAL telt in OBSERVATIONS_TOTAL en NO_SIGNAL_COUNT. Telt NIET in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS_TOTAL, NIET als HIT/MISS/FLAT, NIET in favorable/adverse excursion. Geen hindsight "correct abstention" score. Geen missed-opportunity penalty (geen frozen opportunity-contract).

OBSERVATIONS_TOTAL:
aantal samples in de frozen population met een geldige decision (NO_SIGNAL+LONG+SHORT); = population_total. MISSING_OUTCOME-samples behouden hun decision en tellen mee in observations.

ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS_TOTAL:
LONG_COUNT + SHORT_COUNT.

COVERAGE_FORMULA:
ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS_TOTAL / OBSERVATIONS_TOTAL.

COVERAGE_ZERO_DENOMINATOR:
OBSERVATIONS_TOTAL == 0 → COVERAGE_RATIO.status = NOT_APPLICABLE, value = null, numerator = 0, denominator = 0. Nooit 0.0/1.0/NaN/weglaten. Coverage blijft gescheiden van quality.

DIRECTIONAL_HIT_FORMULA:
LONG: close_delta_pct > 0 → HIT; < 0 → MISS; == 0 → FLAT. SHORT: close_delta_pct < 0 → HIT; > 0 → MISS; == 0 → FLAT. Alleen horizon status == complete draagt bij.

DIRECTIONAL_FLAT_POLICY:
FLAT telt in directional_flat_count (apart gerapporteerd), NIET in HIT/MISS, NIET in de hit-rate denominator. close_delta_pct == 0 is FLAT, geen hit/miss.

DIRECTIONAL_ZERO_DENOMINATOR:
HIT + MISS == 0 (incl. FLAT-only) → DIRECTIONAL_HIT_RATE.status = NOT_APPLICABLE, value = null, numerator = 0, denominator = 0. directional_flat_count blijft apart gerapporteerd. Nooit 0.0/1.0/NaN/weglaten.

LONG_FAVORABLE:
max_up_pct.

LONG_ADVERSE:
max_down_pct.

SHORT_FAVORABLE:
max_down_pct.

SHORT_ADVERSE:
max_up_pct.

HORIZON_ELIGIBILITY:
enkel horizon status == complete is eligible voor directional + excursion quality metrics. partial → PARTIAL_HORIZON exclusion; missing → MISSING_HORIZON exclusion; beide geteld met reason code, nooit als win/loss/zero gescoord.

MISSING_OUTCOME_EFFECT:
sample blijft in population + decision counts (observations_total, LONG/SHORT/NO_SIGNAL). Excluded van alle quality metrics (geen Outcome evidence). Niet zero-fill, niet als MISS/FLAT, geen excursie=0. Reden-code MISSING_OUTCOME in exclusion tally.

PARTIAL_HORIZON_EFFECT:
horizon excluded van quality metrics met reason PARTIAL_HORIZON, per-horizon tally. Andere horizons van dezelfde sample blijven eligible. Geen global sample-flag.

MISSING_HORIZON_EFFECT:
horizon excluded met reason MISSING_HORIZON, per-horizon tally. Niet gescoord.

SUMMARY_STATISTICS:
COUNT, MEAN, MEDIAN (enkel deze; geen extra percentielen).

EMPTY_DISTRIBUTION_POLICY:
N == 0 → COUNT = 0, MEAN.status = NOT_APPLICABLE / MEAN.value = null, MEDIAN.status = NOT_APPLICABLE / MEDIAN.value = null. Per bucket onafhankelijk; maakt geen andere buckets ongeldig.

EVEN_N_MEDIAN_POLICY:
(lower_middle + upper_middle) / 2 van de oplopend gesorteerde finite waarden; odd N → middelste waarde.

FINITE_ONLY:
yes — NaN en ±inf deterministisch geweigerd (zie §14 matrix). Enkel finite numerieke waarden in de distributie. N>0 met alle waarden exact 0.0 blijft geldig (MEAN=0.0, MEDIAN=0.0).

CANONICAL_AGGREGATION_ORDER:
(pair, snapshot_id, asof_ts, decision_id, outcome_record_identity) met outcome_record_identity = (outcome_id, record_id, record_revision). Geen filesystem/dict/set-volgorde. Sommen/means in deze volgorde. Presentatie-rounding niet vóór identity.

EVIDENCE_STATUS_WITHOUT_POLICY:
DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY (altijd zolang geen actieve evidence policy bevroren is; SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verboden, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE niet automatisch op basis van niet-bestaande drempel).

MIN_SAMPLE_THRESHOLD:

CORRELATED_SAMPLE_POLICY:
NEEDS_EVIDENCE

STATISTICAL_INDEPENDENCE_CLAIMED:
no

BREAKDOWNS_REQUIRED:
pair, direction, horizon (combineerde samenvatting mag alleen náást deze subgroepen, nooit ter vervanging).

METRIC_SET_VERSION:
1 (voorstel; exact te bevestigen bij implementatie-candidate).

METRIC_SET_BINDS:
directional HIT/MISS/FLAT semantiek; zero-denominator policy; favorable/adverse normalisatie (LONG/SHORT); COUNT/MEAN/MEDIAN definities (incl. even-N median); canonical aggregation order; finite-number policy.

EVALUATION_CONFIG_V1_FIELDS:
schema_version, strategy_id, strategy_version, batch_id, metric_set_version, selected_horizons, evidence_policy_version/config, missing_data_policy_version, evaluation_purpose. (Geen PID/wall-clock/host/timing.)

SELECTED_HORIZONS_POLICY:
caller declareert selected_horizons expliciet (subset van frozen ALLOWED_WINDOWS 5m/15m/60m/240m). Geen automatische default naar alle vier; geen hidden best-horizon selection. selected_horizons is identity-bound.

EVALUATION_PURPOSE_POLICY:
gereserveerde enum EXPLORATION / VALIDATION / HOLDOUT / OPTIMIZATION; opgeslagen als provenance. OPTIMIZATION ≠ dat er een optimizer bestaat. Een EXPLORATION-resultaat mag later niet als HOLDOUT gepresenteerd worden. Purpose verandert evidence-sufficiency niet.

PRIMITIVE_RESULT_V1_FIELDS:

RESULT_IDENTITY:

OUTCOME_REVISION_TRANSITIVELY_BOUND:
